obligations.description: Clock, synchronous reset, and validity domains
obligations.setup: First set rst_i=1 between edges, hold it across 3 rising edges, then release it on a falling edge; also insert short pulses that do not span a rising edge and resets that span an edge during operation.
obligations.stimulus: Apply resets spanning an edge separately at power-up, during instruction-fetch waits, during data waits, and in the halted state; short pulses occur only between two rising edges.
obligations.expected: The input-history model accepts reset only on rising edges, expecting the next fetch address to be 0, no pending responses, and halt/trace cleared; short pulses do not clear existing state.
obligations.sampling: Accept before the rising edge and sample valid ports stably 1ns after the edge; observe synchronous-reset short pulses between edges.
obligations.checker: Use an input-history interpreter or independent relational prediction, compare valid ports using four-state logic, and report errors; use activity counts to prevent vacuity.

obligations.setup: Start from reset address 0 and maintain the address of each accepted request using an external program image.
obligations.stimulus: Alternate ready between 0 and 1, delay responses by 1 to 6 cycles, hold responses until ready, and continuously execute ordinary instructions with different encodings.
obligations.expected: An independent transaction scheduler calculates request addresses, waiting/buffering, and advancement times; compare valid/ready cycle by cycle, compare addresses at handshakes, and check for duplicate acceptance or lost instructions.
obligations.sampling: Accept before the rising edge and sample valid ports stably 1ns after the edge; observe synchronous-reset short pulses between edges.
obligations.checker: Use an input-history interpreter or independent relational prediction, compare valid ports using four-state logic, and report errors; use activity counts to prevent vacuity.

obligations.setup: Use legal immediates and LUI to establish zero, positive numbers, negative numbers, the highest bit, and all-ones patterns; subsequent STORE instructions output the computation results onto the native data bus.
obligations.stimulus: Execute all 15 R-type instructions, 7 I-type instructions, and LUI, covering shifts by 0/15/16/31, 32-bit overflow, equality/inequality, signed and unsigned ordering, writes to r0, and reads from r0.
obligations.expected: An independent integer arithmetic interpreter calculates the register image and subsequent STORE data, checking the PC and original instruction for each retire; it does not read internal registers.
obligations.sampling: Accept before the rising edge and sample valid ports stably 1ns after the edge; observe synchronous-reset short pulses between edges.
obligations.checker: Use an input-history interpreter or independent relational prediction, compare valid ports using four-state logic, and report errors; use activity counts to prevent vacuity.

obligations.setup: Initialize the external data memory image with patterns such as 80FF807F and FEDCBA98; establish base address 4096 through the program.
obligations.stimulus: Five load types, three store widths, byte offsets 0..3, legal halfword offsets 0/2, negative offsets, overwriting and readback, and immediate use after a load.
obligations.expected: An independent byte array calculates addresses, strobes, write data, and extended values; observe load results externally through STORE instructions following loads, and compare all valid data requests.
obligations.sampling: Accept before the rising edge and sample valid ports stably 1ns after the edge; observe synchronous-reset short pulses between edges.
obligations.checker: Use an input-history interpreter or independent relational prediction, compare valid ports using four-state logic, and report errors; use activity counts to prevent vacuity.

obligations.setup: The program executes a LOAD, an immediately dependent ALU instruction, and a STORE, and also executes a CSR instruction followed by a dependent instruction; externally delay data responses.
obligations.stimulus: Request backpressure of 1 to 5 cycles, response delays of 1 to 10 cycles, dependencies on rs1 and rs2, nondependent instructions, and same-cycle response/subsequent advancement.
obligations.expected: The independent interpreter updates the architectural image on completion events, then schedules dependent execution; compare complete request payloads and retire times, without substituting coverage hits for checking.
obligations.sampling: Accept before the rising edge and sample valid ports stably 1ns after the edge; observe synchronous-reset short pulses between edges.
obligations.checker: Use an input-history interpreter or independent relational prediction, compare valid ports using four-state logic, and report errors; use activity counts to prevent vacuity.

obligations.setup: Establish equal operands, positive and negative operands, and operands with reversed unsigned ordering; place recognizable side effects at skipped locations, and output link values through STORE.
obligations.stimulus: Taken/not-taken outcomes for six branch types, positive and negative offsets, J/JAL/JR/JALR, link rd boundaries, and aligned and misaligned jump targets.
obligations.expected: An independent ISA interpreter calculates the next PC, link values, and exceptions; compare fetch addresses, retirement sequences, and valid STORE operations, confirming that flushed instructions have no side effects.

obligations.checker: Use an input-history interpreter or independent relational prediction, compare valid ports using four-state logic, and report errors; use activity counts to prevent vacuity.

obligations.expected: Request generation tags from input history determine response validity and independently predict the commit sequence; confirm cycle by cycle that no stale instruction produces retire/STORE.
obligations.sampling: Accept before the rising edge and sample valid ports stably 1ns after the edge; observe synchronous-reset short pulses between edges.
obligations.checker: Use an input-history interpreter or independent relational prediction, compare valid ports using four-state logic, and report errors; use activity counts to prevent vacuity.

obligations.description: Illegal instructions, instruction-fetch errors, and alignment exceptions
obligations.setup: First set tvec, then, through a legal peer, separately return an illegal encoding, an instruction-fetch error, and a misaligned operation.
obligations.stimulus: Single errors and combinations of instruction-fetch error with legal misaligned/trap encodings; different low address bits for byte/halfword/word accesses.
obligations.expected: The interpreter calculates priority and cause/badaddr/EPC from input encodings/error bits, compares trap cycle by cycle, and confirms that the instruction produces no retire/data side effects.
obligations.sampling: Accept before the rising edge and sample valid ports stably 1ns after the edge; observe synchronous-reset short pulses between edges.
obligations.checker: Use an input-history interpreter or independent relational prediction, compare valid ports using four-state logic, and report errors; use activity counts to prevent vacuity.

obligations.setup: Issue a LOAD or STORE at a legal aligned address, and externally record the handshake.
obligations.stimulus: Return error separately for reads and writes, covering delayed errors after backpressure and alternating normal/error responses.
obligations.expected: At the actual response acceptance edge, compare cause5/7, the original address, absence of retire, and redirection; the subsequent program confirms through STORE that no erroneous load writeback occurred.
obligations.sampling: Accept before the rising edge and sample valid ports stably 1ns after the edge; observe synchronous-reset short pulses between edges.
obligations.checker: Use an input-history interpreter or independent relational prediction, compare valid ports using four-state logic, and report errors; use activity counts to prevent vacuity.

obligations.setup: Establish a known CSR/counter mirror from reset, configure it through CSRW, and read it out using CSRR+STORE.
obligations.stimulus: All 11 read addresses, 4 write addresses, illegal reads and writes, misaligned EPC/tvec inputs, differences between cycle and instret, and r0 as the destination register.
obligations.expected: The independent image accumulates on each cycle and on successful completion; compare externally exposed STORE data and illegal-access exceptions, without reading internal CSRs.
obligations.sampling: Accept before the rising edge and sample valid ports stably 1ns after the edge; observe synchronous-reset short pulses between edges.
obligations.checker: Use an input-history interpreter or independent relational prediction, compare valid ports using four-state logic, and report errors; use activity counts to prevent vacuity.

obligations.description: Trap entry, MRET, and status priority
obligations.setup: Set tvec; the handler reads EPC/cause/status through CSRR and performs STORE, then modifies EPC and uses MRET to return to the specified continuation address.
obligations.stimulus: EBREAK, TRAP with different immediates, combinations of software traps and IE, MRET round trips, EI/DI, and CSR writes.
obligations.expected: An independent state stack calculates EPC/IE/MPIE, targets, and counters; check that traps do not retire, that MRET retires, and that the restored address is correct.
obligations.sampling: Accept before the rising edge and sample valid ports stably 1ns after the edge; observe synchronous-reset short pulses between edges.
obligations.checker: Use an input-history interpreter or independent relational prediction, compare valid ports using four-state logic, and report errors; use activity counts to prevent vacuity.

obligations.expected: Independent transaction history determines the oldest unexecuted PC and the state stack; compare trap/cause, whether halted, the fetch target, and concurrency with retire; the handler reads back EPC through CSR.
